summary: Luke Badiali ran the opening session with Daniel Reese and Amira Khan. Fernhill keeps losing founder-led software deals to larger growth funds offering bigger cheques. We agreed to focus on Northern founders who want a minority partner and do not want to give up control.

discussion.keyPoints: Amira listed 9 lost deals in 18 months; 6 went to London funds writing £25m-plus cheques. Daniel said Fernhill was often liked but outbid.
Wins came from founders outside London who valued a local, hands-on minority investor and a small board seat rather than control.
Daniel worried that narrowing geography would cut the deal pool too far.

recommendations.recommendation: Target founder-led software and tech-enabled services businesses with £3m to £15m revenue, growing 30% or more, and no prior institutional money.
Prioritise founders in the North West, Yorkshire and the Midlands, with up to 25% of deals elsewhere in the UK.
Position as the minority-only growth partner that never takes control, against majority-seeking PE.
Avoid competitive processes run by London advisers with more than 4 bidders.
Do not match larger funds on valuation; offer a cheque of £5m to £20m with a lighter term sheet instead.

actions.action: Pull the list of 9 lost deals with winning bidder and valuation

nextFocus: Build the founder value proposition around minority-only investment.
nextPreparation: Amira to bring feedback quotes from founders in recent wins and losses.
